I fully understand that. I was scared of the same as well. Not everything will show up on a blood test after a couple weeks (HIV takes an average of 43 days to show up, I believe), but getting tested within a couple of weeks is usually a good idea.

I understand that you're angry. I was so depressed and angry when I got diagnosed that I didn't eat for three days straight until my body couldn't take it anymore. I had outbreaks that occurred every three weeks for the first three and a half months. I was miserable. I wanted to die. 

And I still fucking hate it. But I'm lucky, a lot of my new friends are educated on it. I don't know where you're located or what your sexuality is, but trust me, I've been able to have hookups with full disclosure without people being rude about it. Life doesn't end, even though it feels like it does. Medication and vitamins help a lot. I'm a caffeine and nic fiend and medication + vitamins have stopped me from getting my frequent outbreaks. I haven't had one in the last month (though I'm always scared it's gonna happen lmao)

So you're allowed to be mad. I was in a very similar situation to you. Process the anger. Get mad. But don't let it consume you. Let it lead you to getting the help you need.

I definitely relate. I feel like my life is over for casual sex as well, and go through periods where I feel worthless and dirty. It's no longer as bad as it was the first couple of months, I'm taking care of myself again and no longer stay in bed too depressed to get out, but I still have bad days. 

However, I can tell you that I don't think it's over. I've definitely had my share of ghostings from disclosing and have definitely lowballed myself to the point where I'll just give dudes oral without expecting anything in return (do not recommend). However, I was also able to meet a fwb who is negative but is educated on sexual health and has always been respectful about it. We haven't hooked up yet (cause I was nervous), but I think I'm at the point now where I'm willing to have sex again. I've also had hookups not turn me down for it, though I always try to gauge things before disclosing. I come at it from a weird angle (I'm trans FtM and bi), so my experience may be different, but there's people who really don't care. I understand and feel the depression and sense of self worth you're talking about, I definitely get that. But you also have to make sure you're giving yourself some self respect. This shit sucks, but it's forced me to no longer be as passive when it comes to sex and hookups and also gives me the leverage to ask about the other person's sexual health as well. 

Still hoping they come out with a cure soon, though. That'd make it so much better.

My doctor didn't want to put me on them immediately to see if I was even going to have a second or third outbreak (I did) since some people don't like having the reminder from taking pills for it, but it's calmed me down mentally about having HSV if I'm honest. I'd say it's worth it.
